title: Skill frontmatter
$comment: Source: agents/reference/docs/frontmatter-contract.md#skills. Keep in sync with inventory_frontmatter.py and the linter's lint_skill().

name.description: Lowercase, hyphenated slug; must match the parent directory name.

user-invocable.description: Claude Code Agent-Skills extension: false = the skill claims no /name slash command (only the model can load it). REQUIRED (false) when name equals a Claude Code built-in command or bundled skill (see scripts/_lib/claude_builtin_names.ts) so the suite never shadows the host's own /name. Other tools ignore the key.

description.description: Trigger phrase; the ceiling is 200 chars, measured. Lowered from 220 on 2026-08-22 because 220 described no artefact that existed: across all 290 skills the distribution was median 181 / p75 189 / max 200, with ZERO over 200, so the 20 chars above the recommended line were dead headroom a future author could fill with no gate objecting. p75 = 189 is the recorded soft target; 200 is the hard line. Descriptions load eagerly via progressive disclosure, so every char here is standing cost on every spawn.

compatibility.description: DEPRECATED (announced 2026-08-14, removal maintainer-scheduled — see docs/MIGRATION.md § Scheduled deprecations). Agent-Skills spec field (optional): free-text declaration of environment requirements — system packages, network access, product/host constraints. Superseded by `harness_compat` (the machine-readable class) plus `runtime_requires` (the probeable detail). Still accepted and still emitted so the public-spec mirror keeps working during the window; new skills declare `harness_compat` instead.

harness_compat.description: Structured replacement for the free-text `compatibility` class claim: WHAT KIND of harness constraint the skill carries, in a form `doctor`/`preflight` can branch on. Distinct from `runtime_requires`, which names WHICH bins/env/network to probe — a Python module such as `python-docx` is not a PATH binary, so it has no `bins` entry and would otherwise be invisible to any machine reader. Deliberately single-valued: the enum is derived from the only two skills that ever declared `compatibility`, and both attest exactly one class. A second value is added when a skill attests one, never pre-emptively — a speculative vocabulary is the pro-forma-field risk this schema already refuses for `runtime_requires`. `consumer-installed-deps` = the skill runs only where the consumer has itself installed named third-party libraries or engines; this package ships no runtime for it.
harness_compat.$comment: road-to-skill-ecosystem-executable-payloads Phase 1, under the maintainer's 2026-08-14 resolution of blocker `compatibility-deprecation-is-a-consumer-visible-decision`: ADDITIVE — `harness_compat` lands beside `compatibility`, which is NOT removed here; its removal is approved in principle and scheduled through docs/MIGRATION.md § Scheduled deprecations, never dropped silently. Enum evidence (verbatim, the complete population of `compatibility` users): docx-authoring — "Requires a consumer-installed OOXML library (python-docx …) … Ships zero runtime in this package."; pdf-tools — "Requires consumer-installed PDF libraries: pypdf …, reportlab …; an OCR engine (e.g. tesseract) … Ships zero runtime in this package." Both state one class; the label generalises "library"/"engine" to "deps" and adds no claim neither text makes.

runtime_requires.description: Structured runtime prerequisites, in the form `doctor`/`preflight` can actually probe. The free-text `compatibility` field above states requirements for a human reader; this states them for a machine, and the two coexist deliberately — `compatibility` mirrors the public Agent-Skills spec and is not replaced here. Mandatory for an external `execution.handler` (shell/node/php), which cannot run without declared dependencies; meaningless for `internal`, which by definition needs no external binary. NOT named `requires`: that key is taken by ADR-015 pack-dependency edges (a list of pack ids, validated in build_discovery_manifest.ts), and reusing it makes every skill carrying one unassignable in the discovery manifest.

bins.description: Executables that must resolve on PATH (e.g. `python3`, `curl`). Probed by name, never by version — a version constraint belongs in the skill body where it can explain itself.

env.description: Environment variable NAMES that must be set. Names only — a value here would be a credential in a tracked file (secret-vcs-guard).

primary_env.description: The one variable from `env` whose absence makes the skill unusable rather than degraded, so a doctor report can distinguish a hard block from a partial one. Must also appear in `env`. HALF-ENFORCED, stated plainly: the `dependencies` keyword below requires `env` to be present whenever `primary_env` is, which is the part JSON Schema can express. That the named variable is a MEMBER of `env` is NOT checked anywhere — the linter reads frontmatter by regex, and a fragile pattern on a blocking rule is worse than an honest gap. Zero skills use the field today; the membership check belongs in the doctor wiring (Phase 1, gated on S0.3), where the value is parsed rather than matched.

network.description: Egress hostnames the skill contacts, checked against the egress allowlist. An empty array is a positive claim of no network access and is NOT the same as omitting the key.

runtime_requires.$comment: road-to-skill-ecosystem-executable-payloads Phase 1 (defect D2): `compatibility` is free text used by 2 skills, so cmd_doctor.ts / cmd_preflight.ts had nothing structured to verify. Named `runtime_requires` because `requires` is reserved for ADR-015 pack edges. The `dependencies` keyword closes the half of the primary_env invariant a schema can express; R2 review finding 1 flagged the fully-unenforced version as the same ADR-127 shape this roadmap is closing.

provenance.description: Catalog source attribution: absent or 'official' = maintainer-authored; 'community' = merged external contribution (credited in CREDITS.md; rendered in the catalog's source column).

domain.description: Skill classification axis; see docs/contracts/skill-domains.md. Required for every skill — exactly one of: engineering, product, quality, devops, process, discovery.

framework.description: Framework carve-out marker. Set on skills that are 100% coupled to one stack (e.g. `framework: laravel` on laravel-* skills). Generic, multi-stack skills MUST omit this key. Routed by .agent-src.uncondensed/rules/framework-neutrality-in-generic-skills.md (Tier 2).

tier.description: Optional tier marker. `senior` opts the skill into the Senior-Tier Required Structure check (Context-First lead, Related Skills, Proactive Triggers, Output Artifacts) per .agent-src.uncondensed/rules/skill-quality.md.

meta_skill.description: Opt-out of the linter's `skill_too_large` warn for skills whose purpose IS breadth (skill-writing, agent-docs-writing, skill-reviewer). Meta-skills inherently bundle multiple procedures and inline examples. Use sparingly — every meta_skill: true is a load-on-context trade-off.

external_source.description: SHA-pinned upstream URL for skills adopted under the Reference-Guideline Sunset Policy split path (skill body links to upstream reference modules). Required together with `refresh_trigger` and `sunset_criterion`.

refresh_trigger.description: Event that mandates a rewrite of this skill (e.g. upstream major rewrite, dispatch table reshape, SHA pin invalidation). Required when `external_source` is set.

sunset_criterion.description: Conditions under which the skill should be archived and replaced with a 50-line pointer (e.g. all referenced modules adopted as project-local guidelines, dispatch logic moved to a project-native router). Required when `external_source` is set.

model_tier.description: Vendor-neutral capability band the skill needs (ADR-035, amended by ADR-232). frontier/high/medium/lite project to a native Claude `model:` when model.auto_switch=auto; the generator owns that mapping exclusively. inherit keeps the session model. `frontier` means reasoning capability above the strongest generally-recommended band - opt-in and expected to stay rare, so work that genuinely needs it says so instead of inheriting it silently. Non-Claude agents are suggestion-only - the model-recommendation rule names the tier and the agent resolves its own model. No vendor model names here.

context.description: Optional orthogonal modifier (ADR-035): the skill needs a large-context model regardless of reasoning tier (e.g. summarising a 500-page log). Sparse — most skills omit it. Metadata only; does not change the native Claude `model:` (the tier owns the model choice).

effort.description: Optional pinned reasoning-effort level for hosts with an effort knob (Claude Code `--effort` / agent frontmatter). Passthrough: skills project verbatim, so the key reaches Claude Code as-is and is inert on hosts without the knob. The bench harness pins it per run (bench_ab_task_runner `--effort`) so measurements are reproducible. Orthogonal to `model_tier` (capability band) — effort tunes how hard the model thinks, not which model runs. Omit unless the skill measurably needs a non-default effort.

council_depth.description: Optional reasoning-depth marker for AI Council invocations triggered by this skill. The only accepted value is 'deep'; omit the key for default depth (setting 'standard' is rejected — every frontmatter byte counts against the context window, and 'standard' is the implicit default). 'deep' instructs the host agent to pass --depth deep to council_cli, which floors rounds at max(ai_council.deep_min_rounds, ai_council.min_rounds). Use for architecture, refactoring, or bug-diagnosis skills. See .agent-src.uncondensed/skills/ai-council/SKILL.md.

context_spine.description: Senior-skill opt-in for the context spine. Declares which slots under agents/context-spine/ the skill expects to read. Cross-wing slots (product, team, repo) are locked at 3 by council Q1 (KEEP-3); wing-scoped slots follow the per-wing ADR track in docs/contracts/context-spine.md § 5. Wing-3 (channel-stage, funnel-stage, customer-segment) authorized by docs/contracts/adr-gtm-context-spine.md; Wing-4 (fiscal-period, org-stage, regulatory-regime) authorized by docs/contracts/adr-wing4-context-spine.md.

recommended_for_user_types.description: Forward-compatible user-type recommendation tags (step-12-universal-os-reframe Phase 5). Skill loads for every user-type whose slug appears in this list. Absence of the key marks the skill as universal — see docs/contracts/universal-skills.md for the always-loaded floor and docs/contracts/router-blending.md for per-user-type mix ratios. Wired by step-9-user-types-axis once it lands; treated as metadata until then. Free-form tags (e.g. 'creator', 'founder', 'consultant', 'gtm', 'finance', 'ops', 'developer') — no enum until the user-types axis closes.

allowed_tools.description: Allow-list of tool grants. Prefer the scoped-grant syntax over bare tool names where the host supports it — e.g. Bash(npm test:*) instead of Bash — per tool-safety Least Agency.

disallowed_tools.description: U3 (ecosystem harvest): optional deny-list layered UNDER allowed_tools — defense-in-depth; a tool matching here is refused even if a broad allow pattern would admit it. Supports the scoped-grant syntax (e.g. Bash(git push:*)).

requires_confirmation.description: Optional, additive: the skill's action STAGES rather than executes, so an irreversible step waits for an explicit human confirmation naming the exact object (non-destructive-by-default § Never act while asking). A declaration only — it names the action class, never the object, which exists at stage time and not in frontmatter. The mechanism is stageAction/confirmOnce in work_engine/hooks/builtin/staged_confirmation.ts; enumerate what is pending with `agent-config gates --pending`. Nothing BINDS on this flag yet: only claude both binds pre_tool_use and honours a deny (docs/contracts/hook-architecture-v1.md, section Which hosts carry pre_tool_use — 2 further hosts bind it and ignore the verdict, 3 alias it unbound, 2 have no pre-tool surface), so a guard would degrade to prose on 7 of 8 hosts while the flag reads like a control — that decision is deferred behind blocker confirmation-degraded-host-semantics.

scope.description: OPTIONAL write-scope declaration. Measured 2026-08-23: 0 of 292 SKILL.md files said WHERE a skill may write — `execution:` carries type / handler / timeout_seconds / allowed_tools and `trust:` carries level / removable / default, and none of them answers that question. This is a DECLARATION and a census, not a runtime control: nothing observes a skill's writes, `skill_linter` validates the SHAPE only, and absence stays legal. Saying so is the point — an optional field described as if it constrained anything would be exactly the coverage inflation this repository's enforcement doctrine forbids. Derive it, never guess it: for `handler: shell` the `command:` array names the script whose writes ARE the scope; for `handler: internal` and for a bare `type: manual` the skill executes nothing itself, so an empty `write` list plus a `verification_reason` is the accurate declaration rather than a placeholder.

read.description: Repo-relative globs the skill reads. Optional — omit rather than guess; an invented read set is worse than an absent one.

write.description: Write paths this skill's OWN execution touches. An empty list is a real statement — "this skill declares no write path of its own" — and is falsified by any write its execution performs.

pattern.description: Repo-relative glob the skill may write.

access.description: Closed enum. `create` = new paths only · `write` = create or overwrite · `append` = never rewrites existing bytes · `delete` = removes paths. A value outside the enum is a skill_linter error.

verification_command.description: The command that proves the declared scope is what the skill actually touches. Exactly one of `verification_command` / `verification_reason` is present when `scope:` is — enforced by skill_linter's `scope_verification` check, not by this schema, because JSON Schema cannot express "exactly one of these two optional siblings" in a form this repo's frontmatter validator implements.

verification_reason.description: An HONEST NULL at declaration level: why no command can prove this scope. The pair is deliberately TWO sibling keys rather than a nested `verification: {command|reason}` map, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic: this repo's frontmatter parser reads map -> list -> map (that is how `triggers[].keyword` works) but flattens map -> map -> scalar, so a nested `verification.reason` parses as `scope.verification = ""` plus a stray `scope.reason` and the schema then rejects a correctly-written declaration. A field the parser cannot read is a field nothing validates.

triggers.description: Activation triggers for the SKILL catalogue, shaped after the rule-side field so the two stay legible together — same five match keys (keyword, phrase, file_pattern, path_prefix, command), same additionalProperties:false, and deliberately no `intent` key, which was removed rule-side for giving authors false confidence that an activation path existed. OPTIONAL and empty of adopters on the day it ships: the capability becomes declarable before anything declares it, so a seeded tranche is measurable against the router corpus before it is written. Read by scripts/trigger_coverage.ts --scope skill through the same router_match.ts matcher the rule scope uses — not a fork. Schema: docs/contracts/rule-router.md.

workspaces.description: ADR-013 workspace ids (additive discovery axis). Closed vocabulary enforced by scripts/lint_artefact_frontmatter.py against config/discovery/workspaces.yml.

packs.description: ADR-013 pack ids (additive discovery axis). Closed vocabulary enforced by scripts/lint_artefact_frontmatter.py against config/discovery/packs.yml.

composition_review.description: The authoring-search record (road-to-composition-before-creation Phase 3): which incumbents were searched before this artefact was created, and the declared delta for each. Optional on existing artefacts by design — nothing is backfilled. Distinct from `collision_ok`, which is keyed by trigger VALUE and fires only on a trigger collision; this is keyed by INCUMBENT and is written at authoring time whether or not any trigger is shared.

candidate.description: The incumbent searched, as `skill:<name>` / `rule:<name>` / `command:<name>` / `guideline:<path>`. The literal `none` records a search that found no credible incumbent — the value that must exist so an author is never pushed to invent one to satisfy the schema.

disposition.description: What happened to this candidate. `create_separate` is the value no other disposition vocabulary in this tree can express: an incumbent exists, was evaluated, and a separate artefact was authored anyway.

rationale.description: One sentence naming the delta — what this artefact does that the candidate does not, or why the candidate could not absorb it. A lint checks that this is non-empty and that `candidate` resolves; it cannot check that the search was diligent, and does not pretend to.

requires_skills.description: Skill-composition graph (roadmap 3.4): names of sub-skills this skill's body invokes/assumes. Distinct from ADR-015 `requires` (artefact→pack edges). scripts/check_skill_requires.py enforces (a) each target exists and (b) the required skill is co-available wherever this skill ships (same pack, a requires_hint-reachable pack, or always-on).

trust.description: ADR-013 trust block. Vocabulary mirrored by scripts/lint_artefact_frontmatter.py.

install.description: ADR-013 install hints (default-on at consumer install; user-removable).

token_budget_class.description: Token-cost class for this skill. `lean` (default): subject to telegraph-speak condensation and thin-projector trimming; optimize for <500 tokens. `standard`: balanced guidance, normal condensation. `rich`: exempt from telegraph-speak and thin-projector trimming; detailed examples preserved; eager-load eligible; ≤15% of skills in a suite may be `rich` (CI-enforced). A `rich` skill MUST carry a '## Why this skill is rich' section explaining the irreducible complexity that makes condensation harmful. Governed by `token-budget-discipline` rule + `tokens.rich_skills` consumer setting. See docs/guidelines/token-budget-governance.md.

parallelizable.description: Classifier signal for auto-dispatch. 'steps' = ordered multi-step plan → do-in-steps. 'files' = N independent files of the same shape → do-in-parallel. 'independent' = N independent same-shape targets (not files) → do-in-parallel. Omit for skills that are always single-pass. Read by auto-dispatch-classification.md classifier signal 1.

gaps.description: B6 — honest-null known limitations. Human-curated (NOT auto-discovered), not all skills. Each entry documents a real limitation and cites a witness test that reproduces it. Rendered on the proof page's 'Known Limits'; check_skill_gaps enforces every witness path exists. The offensive-transparency surface a headline-benchmark cannot ship.

description.description: The limitation, stated honestly (what the skill does NOT do / where it fails).

witness.description: Repo-relative path to a test that reproduces/demonstrates this limitation (passes while the gap is real; a failing witness = stale gap to remove).
